body_markdown:
Every[RFP](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/what-is-a-request-for-proposal-rfp) season looks the same. A spreadsheet nobody trusts. A Slack thread asking if anyone has the answer. A deadline that won't move.


Loopio and AutoRFP are often the first platforms teams evaluate while[automating the RFP response process](https://www.inventive.ai/solution/rfp-automation-software) . One is built for governance. The other is built for speed. Choosing the wrong platform can leave your team locked into a year-long contract that doesn't fit its workflow.


This guide compares both platforms on pricing, AI architecture, governance, and support. It is based on verified sales data, G2 reviews, Gartner Peer Insights, and vendor documentation.


***Last reviewed: July 2026.*** *Based on verified sales intelligence, G2, Gartner Peer Insights, and vendor-published materials. Pricing and features change, confirm current specifics directly with each vendor before purchasing.*


## **TL;DR**


- Loopio works for teams that need a governed content library, formal approval routing, and an audit trail.
- AutoRFP works for teams that need a published price, a faster setup, and don't have a dedicated content manager.
- Neither platform is the right fit for every team, the best choice depends on how you manage content, collaborate, and scale proposal operations.


## **What Matters Most When Choosing RFP Software?**


Most RFP platforms can generate responses. The real difference is how they manage content, maintain accuracy, and scale with your team's workflow. Evaluate these six criteria before comparing vendors.


### **1. Content Management**


Every platform depends on accurate company knowledge. The difference is how that knowledge is managed.


- Does it require a structured content library?
- How easy is it to keep answers up to date?
- Can teams quickly find approved content?


If maintaining content becomes a full-time job, adoption often drops over time.


### **2. AI Accuracy**


AI can speed up response drafting, but accuracy matters more than speed.


Look for platforms that help your team:


- Verify AI-generated answers
- Review low-confidence responses
- Reduce outdated or duplicate content


The best AI reduces review time, not just writing time.


### **3. Review and Approval Workflows**


Most RFPs require input from sales, product, legal, security, and compliance.


Ask whether the platform can:


- Assign questions to SMEs
- Track approvals
- Maintain version control
- Support audit requirements


These workflows become increasingly important as proposal volume grows.


### **4. Implementation and Maintenance**


Getting started is only part of the investment. A platform that's quick to deploy but difficult to maintain may create more work later.


Consider:


- Time to onboard
- Content migration effort
- Ongoing library maintenance
- Training requirements


### **5. Integrations**


Your RFP software should fit into your existing technology stack.


Check for integrations with:


- CRM platforms
- Document management systems
- Collaboration tools
- Productivity suites


Strong integrations reduce manual work and improve content reuse.


### **6. Ease of Adoption**


Even the most capable platform delivers little value if teams don't use it consistently.


Look for:


- An intuitive interface
- Minimal training requirements
- Easy SME collaboration
- Workflows that fit existing processes


Higher adoption leads to better content quality and faster response cycles.

## **Loopio Review: Key Features, Limitations, Pricing & Ratings**


[Loopio](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/loopio-pricing-features-reviews) is an RFP response management platform designed for mid-market and enterprise teams managing RFPs,[security questionnaires](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/how-to-answer-a-security-questionnaire) ,[DDQs,](https://www.inventive.ai/solution/ddq-automation-software) and web-based questionnaires. Its core strength is structured content management and proposal governance.


### **Loopio's best features**


- Centralized content library with role-based access controls for approved responses
- **Magic AI** retrieves relevant answers from the content library and uses an OpenAI-powered drafting layer to refine responses
- Confidence scores highlight responses that may require reviewer validation
- Lock approved responses to prevent AI from rewriting compliance-sensitive content
- Go/no-go readiness score shows proposal coverage before submission
- Chrome extension for completing questionnaires directly in customer portals
- Integrates with Salesforce, Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Teams, Word, HubSpot, and Slack


### **Loopio's limitations**


- G2 reviewers report AI drafting works best for repetitive, lower-complexity questions
- Uses OpenAI models for drafting rather than a proprietary LLM
- No inline source citations for AI-generated responses, making verification more manual
- Doesn't automatically detect conflicting answers across the content library
- [G2 reviewers](https://www.g2.com/products/loopio/reviews?qs=pros-and-cons) describe the interface as functional but note a learning curve for occasional users
- User-based pricing can become expensive for organizations with many occasional SME contributors
- Multiple reviewers report the content library requires ongoing maintenance to remain effective as it grows
- Onboarding and professional services may incur additional costs


Via: Loopio


### **Loopio pricing**


Loopio doesn't publish pricing.[Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/loopio) reports contracts ranging from approximately $15,000 to more than $150,000 annually, depending on company size and deployment.

## **AutoRFP.ai Review: Key Features, Limitations, Pricing & Ratings**

## **Loopio vs AutoRFP: Feature-by-Feature Comparison**


Both Loopio and AutoRFP cover the core RFP response workflow, but they take different approaches to AI, content management, governance, and collaboration.


### **AI Capabilities**


#### **Loopio**


- Retrieves approved answers from a structured content library instead of generating responses from scratch
- **Magic AI** matches relevant content and uses OpenAI models to draft or refine responses
- Confidence scores indicate whether a response may require reviewer validation


#### **AutoRFP.ai**


- Uses AI to generate draft responses from your organization's existing knowledge
- Displays a **Trust Score** to indicate confidence in each AI-generated response
- [G2 reviewers](https://www.g2.com/products/autorfp-ai/reviews?qs=pros-and-cons) report a learning curve before teams become comfortable using its AI capabilities


**Key takeaway:** Loopio emphasizes governed content reuse, while AutoRFP.ai prioritizes AI-generated drafting.


### **Knowledge Management**


Both platforms rely on accurate company knowledge, but they manage that knowledge differently.


#### **Loopio**


- Organizes content into a structured library using Stacks, Categories, and Subcategories
- Uses freshness scores to identify content that may need review
- Requires ongoing library maintenance as content grows


#### **AutoRFP.ai**


- Doesn't require a structured content library; learns from approved responses instead
- Reduces the need for manual tagging and library administration
- Still relies on reviewers to keep approved content accurate


**Key takeaway:** Loopio offers more structured governance, while AutoRFP.ai reduces administrative overhead.


### **Conflict Handling**


Conflict detection helps identify when stored answers provide inconsistent information.


#### **Loopio**


- Doesn't automatically detect conflicting answers
- Reviewers must identify and resolve inconsistencies manually


#### **AutoRFP.ai**


- According to AutoRFP.ai, conflicting answers are resolved using recency and context
- Doesn't explain which response was selected or why, limiting reviewer visibility into AI decisions


**Key takeaway:** Loopio leaves conflict detection to reviewers, while AutoRFP.ai automates conflict resolution with limited transparency.


### **Workflow Automation**


#### **Loopio**


- Routes responses through contributors and reviewers
- Includes a go/no-go readiness score to measure proposal completion
- Supports structured approval workflows across multiple departments


#### **AutoRFP.ai**


- Designed for lean teams with lightweight collaboration workflows
- Tracks project progress in real time
- Formal approvals typically happen outside the platform


**Key takeaway:** Loopio supports structured enterprise workflows, while AutoRFP.ai focuses on speed and collaboration.


### **Implementation**


#### **Loopio**


- Standard onboarding typically takes around 30 days
- Teams migrating from manual processes should expect additional time to build and organize a content library
- Onboarding and professional services may incur additional costs


#### **AutoRFP.ai**


- Advertises setup in 48 hours
- Third-party reviews report implementation typically takes several days to weeks


**Key takeaway:** AutoRFP.ai generally offers a faster implementation, while Loopio requires more upfront investment in content management.


### **Integrations**


#### **Loopio**


- Integrates with Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Teams, Word, Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack, and Agentforce
- Strong fit for organizations already invested in the Microsoft and Salesforce ecosystem


#### **AutoRFP.ai**


- Integrates with Salesforce, Google Drive, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and Notion
- Well suited for teams using modern cloud collaboration tools


**Key takeaway:** Loopio provides broader enterprise integrations, while AutoRFP.ai emphasizes lightweight collaboration platforms.


### **Security and Compliance**


#### **Loopio**


- Provides audit trails and enterprise security controls
- Supports data hosting in US and EU regions
- Organizations with strict compliance requirements should request detailed security documentation during evaluation


#### **AutoRFP.ai**


- States[SOC 2](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/inventive-ai-is-now-soc-2-compliant) and ISO 27001 compliance
- States that customer data isn't used to train its AI models
- Security documentation should be requested during vendor evaluation


**Key takeaway:** Both platforms offer enterprise security capabilities, but buyers should validate certifications and documentation during procurement.


### **Analytics**


#### **Loopio**


- Tracks content health, proposal performance, and response completion metrics
- Reporting focuses on content governance and library usage


#### **AutoRFP.ai**


- Reports Trust Scores and productivity metrics
- Reporting is more focused on AI performance than long-term content governance


**Key takeaway:** Loopio provides deeper reporting for content management, while AutoRFP.ai focuses on AI-assisted productivity.


### **Customer Support**


#### **Loopio**


- Includes onboarding with a dedicated Customer Success Manager
- Provides ticket-based support
- Holds a **9.7/10** support score on G2


#### **AutoRFP.ai**


- Provides live chat support
- Doesn't publicly offer a dedicated Customer Success Manager for every account


**Key takeaway:** Loopio offers a more structured enterprise support model, while AutoRFP.ai emphasizes faster day-to-day support.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


**Do Loopio and AutoRFP support security questionnaires and DDQs?** Yes. Both handle RFPs, security questionnaires, and DDQs from the same underlying platform, so you're not choosing a tool that only covers one use case.


**Can you try Loopio or AutoRFP before signing a contract?** Only AutoRFP offers a self-serve option: a 30-day free trial. Loopio's pricing page has no trial, only a "Book a Demo" and a custom quote through sales. If testing the product hands-on before a sales call matters to you, that's a real structural difference between the two.


**Does either platform offer a public API for custom integrations?** Not clearly. AutoRFP.ai lists pre-built connectors for Salesforce, Slack, Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, Confluence, Google Workspace, OneDrive, and Notion, but doesn't publish a dedicated developer API. Loopio's integrations are similarly pre-built rather than open API-based. For anything outside either list, expect a direct conversation with support rather than a self-serve build.


**Do Loopio and AutoRFP support multi-language RFP responses?** Yes, both do, but differently. AutoRFP translates responses across 30+ languages as part of its core workflow. Loopio's multi-language library sits in its Enhanced tier, with full project translation offered as a separate add-on rather than a default feature.


**What user permission levels do Loopio and AutoRFP offer?** Loopio uses four access levels: No Access, Participant, Creator, and Full Access, controlling who can build projects, edit the library, or review responses. AutoRFP uses three roles: User, Content Manager, and Administrator, with granular org-wide controls over project creation, data export, and cross-project content access. Both support confidential/restricted projects for sensitive RFPs.
